adjacent_skills.you_have: UART / I2C / SPI / HID peripheral work
CUDA host/device split, Jetson CPU+GPU pipelines

missing_skills: production-quality embedded software at product scale
required_skills: embedded AI/ML deployment on edge devices
key_responsibilities: Design and optimize embedded AI/ML software for PCs, docks, displays, peripherals
Convert PoC models into production embedded implementations under latency/memory/power constraints
Integrate inference engines, model runtimes and AI accelerators into firmware and system software
Profile and tune embedded AI workloads for inference performance, memory footprint and power
Build software interfaces between AI/ML components, firmware, drivers, sensors, embedded controllers, host apps
Support quantization, pruning, compression, benchmarking and deployment on embedded AI frameworks
Debug system-level issues across AI inference, firmware, sensor data and platform integration
Write architecture, deployment and validation documentation
Explore TinyML, NPU, MCU, sensor fusion and edge inference technologies

strengths: Model optimization for latency/memory is the profile's deepest axis and maps directly onto the JD's core: TensorRT-optimized YOLO on Jetson (56.7 -> 10.9 ms, 17.6 -> 92 FPS, 5.2x over eager PyTorch) and 8-bit LLM.int8() quantization of TinyLlama 1.1B cutting GPU memory ~55% with <1% accuracy loss and +0.09 perplexity.

Inference profiling and benchmarking is evidenced, not claimed: pynvml/psutil peak-VRAM and latency profiling across prompt types, plus HellaSwag/GSM8K/ARC evaluation of the compressed model - exactly the 'benchmarking, regression testing, runtime performance tuning' bullet.

Software interfaces between AI components, firmware, drivers and sensors: COFFIN links Jetson to Arduino over UART inside a WebSocket fabric, drives dual VL53L0X ToF through a TCA9548A I2C mux, and implements two-link IK in C++ on the MCU - the exact AI-to-firmware-to-sensor seam the JD describes.

Memory-constrained bare-metal firmware: STM32 Cortex-M4 monitor written in register-level C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-triggered ADC scan conversion and an interrupt-driven capture path, landing at 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz rate.

System-level debugging across model, firmware and sensor layers: 11 integration failures resolved in COFFIN (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to 10/10 pick reliability at ~11.5 s end-to-end - this is the JD's troubleshooting responsibility verbatim.

Hardware/software co-optimization at the kernel level: custom CUDA C++ conv kernels replacing TorchScript in VGG16 using memory coalescing, constant memory and preallocated global buffers, 49.2 ms vs 77.5 ms CPU baseline.
Deployment as system software rather than a script: Jetson arm bridge shipped as a systemd unit with auto-restart backoff, non-root isolation, environment-file config and static-IP networking.
real_gaps: No NPU, DSP or vendor AI-accelerator SDK work. Every acceleration result in the profile is NVIDIA CUDA/TensorRT. HP commercial client platforms run Intel/Qualcomm/AMD NPUs through OpenVINO, QNN or DirectML, and none of those appear anywhere.
No Windows system software. The role sits inside a Windows commercial-PC stack (WDM/WDF drivers, Windows ML, ETW tracing); the profile's OS work is entirely Linux and bare-metal.
No PC platform internals: boot flow, UEFI/BIOS, firmware interfaces, or the embedded controller (EC) that the JD names explicitly alongside docks, displays and peripherals.

Power and thermal optimization is absent. The JD asks for it three separate times (power consumption, thermal behavior, battery life); the profile optimizes latency and memory and never reports a power or thermal figure.
No secure update mechanism work - signed images, rollback, OTA - which the JD lists under production-quality embedded practice.
CI/CD and automated regression testing for embedded platforms is not evidenced. GitLab and Git appear as version control; no pipeline, no test harness, no regression suite.
Device interconnect stops at UART/I2C/SPI. USB appears only as an Xbox controller Host Shield and HID output; PCIe and Wi-Fi do not appear at all.

Seniority, as prose and not scored here: the JD asks for 7-10 years of relevant experience and the profile is 0 years full-time across capstone, coursework, competition and internship scope. Nothing in it was owned at product scale.
overstated_by_keywords: Pruning - counted as HAVE through the 'model optimization' canonical, but the profile shows 8-bit quantization only. There is no pruning or sparsity artifact anywhere.

Device drivers - resolved 'strong' via peripheral programming, but the evidence is register-level bare-metal peripheral code on STM32/Arduino, not OS-level driver development, which is what the JD means next to Windows and Linux.
TFLite - a one-line export target in the Tusk internship (YOLOv8n to ONNX and TFLite for mobile), not a runtime he integrated or tuned.
Sensor fusion - mapped to 'autonomous systems', but the real evidence is ToF range-gating plus encoder odometry, not a fusion filter over multiple sensor modalities.
RTOS - FreeRTOS with mutexes on the turret project and coursework; working depth, not the production RTOS integration the JD implies.
C/C++ - counted at full weight, but C++ depth is a known live weakness in interviews; the JD wants strong C/C++ as a primary language.
understated_by_keywords: The COFFIN systemd/static-IP/XRDP deployment work is genuine embedded system-software integration and never string-matches any JD keyword.

The STM32 monitor's 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM figure is direct evidence for the JD's 'memory constraints' and 'real-time execution tradeoffs' asks, but reads as a coursework project to a keyword scan.
Robocon's interrupt-driven 4-bit quadrature state machine and fail-safe motor-halt state machine demonstrate deterministic real-time firmware design that no JD term picks up.

The ASR project's Cython-accelerated BPE tokenizer (4-5.5x over pure Python) is data-preprocessing performance engineering - exactly the JD's 'data preprocessing, feature extraction, runtime performance tuning' - but scores nothing.

Accuracy-latency trade-off reporting for deployment appears twice (Teesside U-Net backbones, SLM benchmarking) and is the deployment-decision skill the JD asks for under 'model deployment strategy and validation plans'.
screening_gaps: 7-10 years of relevant experience against 0 years full-time. This is a senior individual-contributor req at $147K-$231K; a new-grad profile is filtered before the skill match is ever read.
No NPU or vendor accelerator SDK experience (OpenVINO, QNN, DirectML). The entire AI acceleration record is NVIDIA CUDA/TensorRT, and HP's client AI silicon is not NVIDIA.
No Windows system-software or PC platform firmware experience - drivers, embedded controller, boot flow, secure update - which is the platform this role integrates into every day.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The model-optimization half of this job is a genuine match: quantization, TensorRT, inference profiling and benchmarking are all backed by specific measured results, and the AI-to-firmware-to-sensor integration seam in COFFIN is the same seam the JD describes. The platform half is not there - NPU/OpenVINO acceleration, Windows system software, PC firmware and EC, and power/thermal tuning are four distinct core areas with no evidence, and they are the areas HP specifically hires this role to own. Worth one application slot on the strength of the edge-inference core, but expect the years-of-experience filter to be the thing that ends it, not the skills.
